## Current signals

- WebNR remains a local-first browser reader and may be described as an independent browser-based alternative for some Legado users and web-first reading workflows. It is unaffiliated with Legado and is not an official Legado web client. Arbitrary Legado source JSON is not yet a drop-in WebNR runtime; compatibility claims remain tied to tested capability levels and versioned fixtures.
- Pull request #141 admits `DBNL Public Domain Discovery Starter` as the 23rd maintained source family. Its first-party rights evidence is unusually strong: DBNL's public-domain collection states that listed titles are copyright-free/public domain and may be used for any purpose, while the selected representative pages are individually marked `Auteursrechtvrij` and expose TXT/XML download options.
- DBNL remains discovery-only at this capability level for a runtime reason, not a rights assumption. WebNR's direct URL import is browser-side and this cycle did not obtain a repeatable browser-CORS result for DBNL `tekstbestand` endpoints. The starter therefore stores only first-party DBNL page URLs plus WebNR-authored labels/descriptions. It does not mirror text, metadata archives, bulk TXT/XML ZIPs, PDFs, ebooks, images, credentials, or cookies. Upgrade to direct TXT requires an actual browser fixture proving CORS, response/timeout bounds, stable identity, update/deletion, and failure behavior.
- The 2026-09-04 new-candidate pass screened DutchDraCor, Liber Liber / Project Manuzio, Projekt Gutenberg-DE, OpenGreekAndLatin / First1KGreek, and Deutsches Textarchiv. DutchDraCor and First1KGreek are strong structured-text candidates but need deterministic TEI-to-reading-text fixtures and license/attribution propagation. Liber Liber requires item-level rights and project-contribution boundaries. Projekt Gutenberg-DE is excluded from content ingestion under its current private-use restrictions. DTA remains deferred because current first-party access/reuse evidence could not be audited reliably without bypassing access controls.
- Rotating health checks on GITenberg Direct TXT Starter, CLiGS Textbox Spanish-American TXT Starter, Project Ben-Yehuda Public Domain TXT Starter, and Folger Shakespeare TXT Starter passed at their currently admitted capability boundaries. No reproducible failure required removal or downgrade.
- Pull request #139 remains the first-month source directory / health report and admitted CLiGS as the 22nd family after a 21/21 prior-family health pass. The CLiGS starter retains exactly three commit-pinned direct-TXT entries from the 19th-century Spanish-American collection and preserves its CC BY 4.0 provenance/attribution boundary.
- Project Ben-Yehuda Public Domain TXT Starter remains a bounded four-entry direct UTF-8 source pinned to audited upstream public-domain dump commit `5e4277fead7b565f32cc4b352abd3565023a77d8`. GITenberg Direct TXT Starter remains a bounded three-entry Git-backed raw-TXT source. Folger Shakespeare TXT Starter remains a bounded three-entry first-party TXT source preserving Folger provenance and the CC BY-NC 3.0 attribution/noncommercial boundary. None of these catalogs is silently widened.
- Link-only is a proven current capability level rather than a permanent policy ceiling. A source moves to direct TXT/API/feed/synchronization only when the richer capability has source-specific rights/access, browser/runtime transport, stable identity, cadence, pagination, resource, attribution, update/deletion, and versioned-fixture evidence.
- `Fanfiction Discovery Starter` remains at eight audited first-party discovery destinations: FanFiction.Net, Fimfiction, Scribble Hub, Archive of Our Own (AO3), SquidgeWorld, fanfiction.lol, Sunset, and Asianfanfics. AO3 canonical-tag Atom remains a richer-interface candidate requiring bounded transport, stable identity, update semantics, response/cadence limits, attribution, and fixtures before synchronization is claimed.
- Fimfiction remains a strong official-API upgrade candidate, but its current developer/application path requires an externally created API application/client identity. WebNR must not fabricate credentials. Once that prerequisite exists, the adapter still requires bounded OAuth transport, rate-limit/backoff, caching, stable identity, cursor pagination, response/timeout bounds, provenance, attribution, update/deletion semantics, and fixtures.
- Pull request #126 remains the versioned Legado baseline: fixture suite `2026-08-30.1` and local-only inspector implement L1 import/inspection. L2 declarative, L3 stateful, L4 script, and L5 Bridge/WebView requirements may be recognized but are not executed. Inspection is bounded to 2 MiB and 500 source definitions and performs no target-site request, login, Cookie, JavaScript, WebView, CAPTCHA, paywall, robots, DRM, or access-control bypass.
- Pull request #127 remains the documentation analytics repair baseline. Reader and documentation output use only `G-DGH8HNQKE4`, require `page_location: window.location.href` and query-bearing `page_path: window.location.pathname + window.location.search`, and keep `allow_google_signals` plus `allow_ad_personalization_signals` false.
- `https://www.webnovel.win/` is the sole canonical public identity for documentation, reader-facing articles, search indexing, canonical tags, sitemap, and RSS. `https://app.webnovel.win/` is the reader application runtime; `https://autoarchive.github.io/webNR/` is an attributable documentation build mirror only.
